standard_prerequisites: Topology, Example topology-example-automorphisms-of-a-set: the compact open topology on Map(E, E) is the universal topology making the action Map(E, E) x E -> E continuous (E discrete), and Aut(E) with the compact open topology is a topological group; cited as standard facts of the sibling Topology chapter
Topology, Lemma topology-lemma-profinite-group: a topological group whose underlying space is profinite is a profinite group
Same chapter: lemma-algebraic-extension-self-map (an F-algebra self-map of an algebraic extension is an automorphism)
core_obligations: The lemma's topology on Gal(E/F) is the induced topology from the injective map Gal(E/F) -> Map(E, E) into the compact open topology; hence the universal property (1) for continuous X x E -> E actions follows from the compact open universal property
Gal(E/F) = Aut(E/F) factors through Aut(E), so the induced structure makes Gal(E/F) a topological group, and by construction the coarsest one with continuous action

Profinite: for finite S subset E the set G(S) of root-respecting maps S -> E is finite; G = lim G(S) over finite S is profinite; the canonical map c: Gal(E/F) -> G is injective with image the closed locus of conditions (A) f_S(alpha) + f_S(beta) = f_S(alpha+beta) and (M) f_S(alpha) f_S(beta) = f_S(alpha beta) (where defined); an element of the image is lim f_S, an F-algebra map E -> E, hence an automorphism; so Gal(E/F) is homeomorphic to a closed subset of a profinite space
proof_roadmap: Identify the lemma's topology with the induced compact open topology and derive the universal property and group structure
Build the finite approximation sets G(S) and the inverse limit G
Characterize the image of c by the closed conditions (A) and (M) and conclude profinite
